title: Teenager Hannah Klugman Wins Her Biggest Tennis Title Yet in Wrexham
summary: British teenager Hannah Klugman has won the biggest title of her tennis career so far, and she did it in style. The 17-year-old beat French player Elsa Jacquemot 6-2 6-4 in the final of the Lexus Wrexham Open. It was a W100 title, and Klugman did not drop a set all week. That is a run to remember. Klugman is now the second British player in a row to win the Wrexham title, after Wales player Mimi Xu won last year. She is also the youngest Briton to win a singles trophy at W100 level or higher. From the very first game, Klugman put pressure on Jacquemot, who is ranked world number 157. She missed her first two chances to break serve, but she did not give up. Just two games later, she got her reward and took control of the match. Even in the biggest match of her career so far, Klugman had to fight to finish the job. Jacquemot battled back to 5-4, and the crowd must have held its breath. Then, at the second time of asking, the home favourite served out the victory. Afterwards, Klugman said, "I was shaking afterwards, but just so, so happy and proud of myself again." It was a moment of pure joy after a week of steady, confident tennis. There was more British success in the doubles final, too. Freya Christie and Eden Silva beat Japan player Hiroko Kuwata and India player Ankita Raina 6-2 6-3. For Klugman, this title is a big step forward. She arrived as a teenager with talent, and she left Wrexham as a champion who had handled the biggest match of her life with courage and calm.
why_it_matters: It shows young players that steady, brave tennis can turn talent into a first big title, and it gives British tennis a new young champion to follow.

background_read: Tennis is a sport in which two players hit a ball back and forth over a net, trying to win points, games, and sets.
A tournament brings many players together, and the winner of the final match takes the trophy.
Winning a title without dropping a set means winning every set played all week, which is a sign of steady, dominant play.
Klugman's win matters because she is a teenager playing at a high professional level, and the Wrexham title has now stayed with British players for a second year in a row.
